item.title: Guwahati to Host Third Edition of Northeast International Documentary & Film Festival on Dec 13
item.description: GUWAHATI: Guwahati will host the third edition of the Northeast International Documentary & Film Festival on December 13 at Jyoti Chitraban Film Studio. The event marks the festival’s return with an expanded format and new partnerships aimed at strengthening its presence in the region. item.title: Allottee Holds Right & Title over Land After Land Passbook Issued by Govt, Rules Gauhati HC
item.description: GUWAHATI: The Gauhati High Court has ruled that once government-allotted land is transferred and the transfer is approved through the issuance of a Government Land Passbook, the allottee continues to hold right and title over the land until the allotment is cancelled or withdrawn by the competent authority. item.title: Tezpur University Gets Acting VC, But Student Protest Continues Over Pending Issues
item.description: GUWAHATI: In a significant administrative development at Tezpur University, Professor Dhruba Kumar Bhattacharyya has assumed charge as the Acting Vice-Chancellor after over 75 days of campus-wide unrest. item.description: GUWAHATI: Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari on Thursday, December 4, announced that India’s existing toll collection system will be replaced by a barrier-less electronic toll system within the next one year, offering seamless travel for highway users. item.title: Two Injured in Guwahati’s Zoo Road Flyover Accident
item.description: GUWAHATI: Two people sustained minor injuries in a road accident on the Zoo Road flyover on Friday morning, December 5. The incident occurred around 9:00 AM when a four-wheeler reportedly lost control and collided with a motorbike approaching from the Ganeshguri side. item.title: Over 1,000 IndiGo Flights Cancelled; Airline Issues Apology Letter
item.description: GUWAHATI: IndiGo’s ongoing operational crisis deepened on Friday, with total cancellations since Tuesday surpassing 1,000 and more than 400 additional flights scrapped this morning, according to national reports. The disruption, now entering its fourth straight day, has left thousands of domestic and international passengers stranded at major airports with minimal updates from the airline. item.title: IndiGo Expects Normal Operations by December 10–15, Says CEO Pieter Elbers
item.description: GUWAHATI: IndiGo is likely to resume normal operations between December 10–15 after a week of strain that peaked on December 5, when chief executive Pieter Elbers also delivered a public apology and acknowledged the scale of the airline’s collapse. The carrier logged more than 1,000 cancellations in a single day, disrupting over half its network and triggering a nationwide backlog. item.title: Assam Relaxes Two-Child Norm for SC, ST, Tea Tribe, Moran and Matak Communities
item.description: GUWAHATI: In a significant policy change, the Assam government on Friday, December 5, relaxed the two-child norm for Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), tea garden communities, Moran and Matak groups, allowing up to three children for eligibility in government employment, elections and Self Help Group (SHG) incentives.
